question: A 40-year-old pregnant woman, G4 P3, visits your office at week 30 of gestation. She is very excited about her pregnancy and wants to be the healthiest she can be in preparation for labor and for her baby. What vaccination should she receive at this visit?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "30 weeks gestation" -> "Tdap recommended in third trimester" -> "protects newborn from pertussis" -> 95%
CHAIN: "30 weeks gestation" -> "live vaccines contraindicated in pregnancy" -> "avoid live attenuated influenza vaccine" -> 90%
CHAIN: "30 weeks gestation" -> "live vaccines contraindicated in pregnancy" -> "avoid varicella vaccine" -> 90%
CHAIN: "30 weeks gestation" -> "live vaccines contraindicated in pregnancy" -> "avoid herpes zoster vaccine" -> 90%
CHAIN: "30 weeks gestation" -> "live vaccines contraindicated in pregnancy" -> "avoid MMR vaccine" -> 90%
analysis: During pregnancy, it is recommended that women receive the Tdap vaccine between 27 and 36 weeks of gestation to protect the newborn from pertussis. Live vaccines, such as the live attenuated influenza vaccine, varicella vaccine, herpes zoster vaccine, and MMR, are generally contraindicated during pregnancy due to potential risks to the fetus.
